newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Taylor names cabinet after Liberia celebrations.
newsitem.headline: Taylor names cabinet after Liberia celebrations.

text.p: Charles Taylor announced key cabinet appointments on Sunday after his inauguration as Liberian president on Saturday, an event that was followed by the war-torn country's biggest party in years.
Festivities went on throughout the night after peacekeepers of the West African ECOMOG force relaxed a seven-year-old curfew.

Taylor supporters were offering free drinks and food in the bars and restaurants of Monrovia, and Taylor himself hosted a banquet for visiting African leaders, including Nigeria's military ruler Sani Abacha.
Taylor issued a statement naming 15 members of a 19-member cabinet, including Elie Saleeby as minister of finance. Saleeby currently works for the World Bank in Washington.

Sandra Howard, who is the sister of Taylor's wife, will be the minister of planning and economic affairs. Taylor's younger brother, Bob, takes over as managing director of the Forestry Development Authority.
Roland Massaquoi retains his position as minister of agriculture, and Jenkins Dunbar continues as minister of lands, mines and energy.
Benoni Urey retains his important junior minister's post as commissioner of the maritime bureau.
Brigadier General Philip Kamah, until now deputy chief of staff of the rump National Army, has been appointed minister of national security.
The new governor of the central bank of Liberia will be Charles Bright.
Taylor, who set off a civil war in Liberia in 1989, won an overwhelming victory in national elections on July 19 to become Liberia's first civilian president in 12 years.
In his inaugural address on Saturday, he repeated a pledge that former rivals would be included in his government and four cabinet slots were left unfilled in Sunday's announcement.
